turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so tell me who decided that and when.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
You didn't answer me. Who entered that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in? Then show me whatever you want me to look at.
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
I didn't say a word about a timestamp. If you have a document with times on it, put it in front of me. Otherwise I'm still waiting to hear who decided.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to." You're leading me, Hale, and I've done this for twenty years. Show me what you have on Owen's essay, or I'm going to the principal when we're done.
